react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal. MetaboAnalystR (KEGG PSEA, p = 5.77e-07) ranked KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) first with six hits: androstenedione, testosterone, DHEA, estrone, 17β-estradiol, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone). RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 4.97e-18) placed KEGG:map00140 and SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at ranks 2 and 1 respectively, each with identical 6-hit, 1501-fold enrichment. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p = 8.40e-05) ranked MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism first; its empirical-compound network expanded the hit set to 14 steroids including the six input sex steroids plus related intermediates (androsterone, estriol, 6β-hydroxytestosterone, etc.), confirming complete pathway saturation. A secondary signal from 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde independently reached mummichog rank 2 (p = 0.029) in tyrosine metabolism, consistent with dopamine-catabolism origin via MAO/ALDH. Warfarin, the single xenobiotic in the input set, did not map to any endogenous pathway and is flagged as a likely medication or experimental confound. The biological story is a coordinated perturbation of the gonadal steroid axis: aromatase (CYP19A1) is the canonical branch-point enzyme converting androstenedione (C00280) to estrone (C00468), while HSD3B/HSD17B enzymes interconvert DHEA, androstenedione, testosterone, and 17β-estradiol. The treatment effect appears to span both androgen and estrogen arms simultaneously, consistent with CYP17A1 or aromatase modulation.
